  path = "../../../crush-ast/crates/crush-lang-sdk"
which assumes the dev layout of ./projects/arniko + ./projects/crush-ast.
Previously the CI checked arniko out to ./arniko and crush-ast to
./crush-ast, so the relative path did not resolve.

Fix: in the arniko-crush job, check arniko out to ./projects/arniko and
crush-ast to ./projects/crush-ast, matching the dev layout so the
relative path dep resolves correctly.

decision_reason: Compared bliss-dom/stylo_taffy/mustang against Servo's layout, script/dom, and compositing for portable techniques. Layout (Taffy bridge): no concrete visible-output bug found; only a lower-confidence note that bliss-dom routes both flex+grid through Taffy (stylo_taffy/convert.rs) while Servo itself only trusts Taffy for grid and hand-rolls flexbox internally (servo components/layout/formatting_contexts.rs, flexbox/). DOM surface: bliss-dom already has event dispatch, getBoundingClientRect, and querySelector — real gaps were classList/dataset/matches()/closest()/MutationObserver vs servo components/script/dom/*. GPU compositing: mustang's SceneScheduler (now living in the standalone nixpt/mustang repo, not arniko) is a single monotonic dirty counter that re-runs all effects on any DOM change (scheduler.rs self-documents this as 'a follow-up'); Servo's paint/painter.rs RepaintReason bitflags + display_list.rs invalidate_cached_transforms show a small, portable per-reason/per-node dirty pattern mustang's own already-implemented but unused Region::union could adopt.

decision_title: ElementData::id orphan-field audit-correction
decision_reason: A prior audit claim asserted that ElementData::id would silently diverge from node.attr(local_name!("id")) after a post-construction DocumentMutator::set_attribute(elem, "id", ...) call. Verified against current crates/bliss-dom/src/mutator.rs::DocumentMutator::set_attribute and ::clear_attribute: both paths handle the id-name case explicitly - set_attribute assigns element.id = Some(Atom::from(value)); clear_attribute assigns element.id = None. The orphan-field hazard as originally described does NOT exist in current main. Three regression tests added to crates/bliss-dom/src/tests/document.rs to lock in the invariant: (1) test_elementdata_id_field_tracks_set_attribute with 4 sub-blocks (construct-time id, post-construction set_attribute, post-construction clear_attribute, empty-string round-trip); (2) test_clear_attribute_does_not_reset_id_for_non_id_attrs - negative companion (clear_attribute("class") must NOT touch element.id); (3) test_elementdata_id_first_set_after_no_id_construction - lifecycle covering None -> Some via set_attribute after no-id construction. cargo test -p bliss-dom --lib --offline returns 47 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored (pre-existing 44 + 3 new). Rejected: SAFETY comment in ElementData::id (the invariant's load-bearing site is the mutator guard, not the field); ElementData::new re-extract-on-set_attribute patch (would mask regressions the tests are designed to catch).

decision_title: D1 round-10 example location: mutate existing round-8 example rather than spawn a new crate
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D1: chose to mutate `examples/multi-tab-log/` rather than spawn a new example crate. Rationale: the round-8 example was already the single end-to-end consumer composing every vendored sibling + the round-9 TabLog helper; adding round-10 as a new crate would split consumer surface across two crates without a clean contract distinction (a new example would re-render the same four-region layout, the same scroll-back log bodies, the same TabNav — nothing new at the example level except a 12-col widget in the footer). The mutation cost is a single Layout::Horizontal split inside draw() + a 12-cell ring buffer field + a 7th smoke test; the gain is a unified consumer surface. This pattern generalizes: future rounds 11+ that compose a vendored widget into an existing example should mutate the corresponding example rather than spawn a parallel crate. Cross-ref: PR #8 (round-8 vendoring) + PR #5 (round-7 scroll-log) + PR #3 (round-1-6 vendoring wave) all shipped with the same mutate-not-split discipline.
summary: Claim: D1 round-10 example location: mutate existing round-8 example rather than spawn a new crate

Diagnostic chain selecting Sparkline over the 6 candidates: Sparkline (Widget-only, lowest lift), Chart (stateful + multi-line metric plot, heaviest), BarChart (mid), Sparkline (selected), Calendar (stateful date grid, specialized), LineGauge (stateful progress bar). decision_title: D4 round-10 keymap: Sparkline is display-only, no keymap / no focus / no selection
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D4: chose to vendor Sparkline as **display-only** — no keymap (`q`/`Esc`/digit-range/etc. do nothing on the widget itself), no focus model, no selection cursor. Diagnostic: upstream Sparkline has no `StatefulWidget` impl and no input-handling surface — vendoring a non-existent surface would force us to invent a contract that no consumer can rely on. Pattern: a future round adopting a stateful widget (Chart, List, Calendar) carries the cost of either a 4th-keymap-region NOR a state-carrier contract — the design memo for that round MUST name which (or both); the round-6 Tabs precedent uses both (state carrier `TornadoState` did not surface because of the E0034 carve-out, but the StatefulWidget pattern is documented for future resume).

decision_title: D5 round-10 layout: 12-col Sparkline slotted into the right flank of the existing 2-row status_bar via Layout::Horizontal split
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D5: chose Layout::Horizontal split inside the footer region `[Min(width-12), Length(12)]` to slot the Sparkline beside the existing text status_bar Paragraph. No top-level layout shift — the same 4-region split (`Title 1 / TabNav 3 / Body Min(3) / Status 2`) is preserved; only an internal horizontal split is added inside status_area. Diagnostic: a body-region slot (charting inside the body) would compete with the TabLog-scroll-view for vertical space; a title-region slot would crowd the brand row. The footer-internal split is the smallest change that opens a new compositional surface without disturbing round 7-8-9 layout investments. Pattern: future round-11 widgets compose with the SHELL by slotting *inside* an existing region, not by adding a sibling 5th region — this keeps the [1, 3, Min(3), 2] layout as the consumer-facing contract. Cross-ref: round-9 TabLog helper consumed many round-7 helper signatures while keeping the same 4-region layout.
summary: Claim: D5 round-10 layout: 12-col Sparkline slotted into the right flank of the existing 2-row status_bar via Layout::Horizontal split

decision_title: D6 round-10 tests: 6 inline + 6 integration + 7th example-app smoke (deterministic ring-state)
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D6: chose to ship 6 inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` inside `crates/tornado-sparkline/src/lib.rs` + 6 gateway integration tests in `crates/tornado-sparkline/tests/sparkline_integration.rs` + a 7th example-app smoke `smoke_sparkline_metrics_advance_on_tick` that exercises the round-10 D9 deterministic-ingestion contract. The 7th test pins the `Instant::now()` test-loop trap defense: it never calls `update()` (the loop that triggers `self.last_tick.elapsed()`); it calls `push_sparkline_metric` with explicit values instead. The 6 inline tests cover the 5 builder methods + the empty-data no-op; the 6 integration tests exercise the public surface from outside the crate (the same way a downstream consumer would reach the widget). Pattern: every vendored sibling should ship (a) inline unit tests for the builder math, (b) gateway integration tests for the public surface stability, (c) at most 1 example-app smoke that pins a constitutional-hazard defense.
summary: Claim: D6 round-10 tests: 6 inline + 6 integration + 7th example-app smoke (deterministic ring-state)

decision_title: D7 round-10 vendoring surface: pub use at lib.rs + widget.rs (no semantic alias like Tabs→TabNav)
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D7: chose to surface the vendored `Sparkline` + `SparklineBar` via `pub use tornado_sparkline as sparkline;` at lib.rs + `pub use crate::sparkline::{Sparkline, SparklineBar};` at widget.rs WITHOUT a semantic rename — no `TabNav`-style alias. Rationale: Sparkline is already the canonical upstream verb and does not need a `TabNav`-style rename (the round-6 catch-up needed the rename because `Tabs` was reserved by upstream *and* by the previous direct import path, creating ambiguity; Sparkline carries no such collision). The mirror is 1:1 with upstream names; consumers reach `tornado::widget::Sparkline` directly. Pattern: the umbrella widget-rename alias is reserved for cases where the upstream name collides with a pre-existing alias or Path B; carry the rename ONLY when the collision exists. Round-6 catch-up is the canonical example requiring the rename; round 10 is the canonical example *not* requiring it.
summary: Claim: D7 round-10 vendoring surface: pub use at lib.rs + widget.rs (no semantic alias like Tabs→TabNav)

Sparkline widgets compose with status_bar footer but NEVER compete with it: Sparkline is a sub-region INSIDE the bar (the right flank via Layout::Horizontal split), not a peer to the bar in the body regions. A future round adopting Sparkline (or any sub-barlike widget) MUST NOT add a 5th top-level region to the consumer layout [Title 1, TabNav 3, Body Min(3), Status 2] — that breaks every existing example-app that consumes the round-7/8/9 contract. decision_title: D9 round-10 ingestion: rolling 12-frame ring + tick_count % TASK_COMPLETE_EVERY == 0 (deterministic + MSRV-portable)
decision_reason: Round-10 design memo D9: chose to ingest metrics via a deterministic 12-cell rolling window Vec<u64> of length SPARKLINE_RING_LEN, advanced by self.push_sparkline_metric(self.tick_count as u64) called from update(). Diagnostic: (a) MSRV portability — <integer>::is_multiple_of is stabilized in Rust 1.87.0 but the workspace pins rust-version = "1.85.0", so the modulo operator count % N == 0 is the only stable form (carries forward the round-8 constitutional hazard #1). (b) Deterministic across CI — tick_count is a u32 field advanced by update() once per loop iteration, so no Instant::now() involvement (carries forward the round-8 constitutional hazard #3). The 12-cell ring fits the footer right-flank 12-col slot exactly so Sparkline::new(&ring) renders one bar per cell. Pattern: update() test loops should tick the underlying state directly with explicit values never relying on wall-clock elapsed (see round-8 smoke_spinner_advances_in_title precedent + round-10 smoke_sparkline_metrics_advance_on_tick).
summary: Claim: D9 round-10 ingestion: rolling 12-frame ring + tick_count % TASK_COMPLETE_EVERY == 0 (deterministic + MSRV-portable)

decision_title: D1 round-11 example location: NEW examples/multi-nav-list/ (NOT a mutation of round-8 multi-tab-log)
decision_reason: Round-11 design memo D1: chose NEW examples/multi-nav-list/ rather than mutating examples/multi-tab-log/. Rationale: List consumes the BODY region as a selected-row navigation surface, structurally different from round-7/8 scroll-log body. Mutating examples/multi-tab-log/ would replace its scroll-log body with a row-based List, breaking the round-7/8/9 contract (the four-region layout, the 5-tab dynamism, the TabLog helper). Round-10 D1 was a sub-region rule (Sparkline slotted INTO the existing footer) and it does NOT extend to top-level body replacement - List is structurally a body-region widget, not a sub-region composition. Diagnostic chain: examples/multi-tab-log/ carries the round-9 TabLog helper which is round-7 scrollview-tail-logic promoted to generic tooling; replacing its body region with List would orphan the scroll-log helper entirely. A new example crate lets the scroll-log surface stay distinct (round-8) while the keyboard-nav navigation surface lands fresh (round-11), giving downstream consumers two non-overlapping reference implementations to choose from.
summary: Claim: D1 round-11 example location: NEW examples/multi-nav-list/ (NOT a mutation of round-8 multi-tab-log)

decision_title: D2 round-11 state model: StatefulWidget parity (Vendor BOTH Widget for List AND StatefulWidget for List PLUS ListState)
decision_reason: Round-11 design memo D2: chose StatefulWidget parity - vendor BOTH Widget for List AND StatefulWidget for List, plus ListState (the selected:Option<usize> + offset:usize carrier). This is a deliberate divergence from round-6 Tabs (which shipped Widget-only + carved-out StatefulWidget due to E0034 ambiguity). Round 11 IS the canonical StatefulWidget-vendoring precedent - every future round adopting a stateful widget (Chart, Calendar, future Pane composites) references round 11 E0034 carve-out pattern (per design memo section 3). Diagnostic: round-10 D2 documented Sparkline is fully display-only because upstream ratatui has no StatefulWidget impl for it; round 11 INVERTS that - List has BOTH impls upstream, so the decision to vendor BOTH is the precedent (not a carve-out). Carry-forward hazard: round-8 E0034 two-step-borrow pattern does NOT apply here (vendored crate compiles cleanly when both impls are in scope; E0034 ambiguity only surfaces at the consumers call site, never in the vendored source code).
summary: Claim: D2 round-11 state model: StatefulWidget parity (Vendor BOTH Widget for List AND StatefulWidget for List PLUS ListState)

decision_title: D3 round-11 surface: List (builder) + ListState (carrier) + ListState::select (no widget-side keymap)
decision_reason: Round-11 design memo D3: surface re-export should mirror ratatui 0.30 verbatim - List (builder widget, stateless per-frame POV), ListState (carrier selected:Option<usize> + offset:usize), builder methods (items, block, style, highlight_style, highlight_symbol, repeat_highlight_symbol, direction), ListState::new() / ::default() / ::select(Option<usize>). NO keymap-on-widget surface - the consumer frame dispatch owns routing (D4); the vendored crate stops at the Widget+StatefulWidget + ListState surface, period. Diagnostic: round-6 catch-up Tabs surface used the same shape (Tabs + builder methods alone, no widget-side keymap) and that worked because the consumer handle_event owns routing. Round 11 inherits this proven pattern. The only NEW surface element vs round-6 is ListState - the canonical selection carrier that round-9-future projections (selection-driven scroll composition, command-palette current-query-match tracking) all reference.
summary: Claim: D3 round-11 surface: List (builder) + ListState (carrier) + ListState::select (no widget-side keymap)

decision_title: D4 round-11 keymap: arrow + vim into ListState::select, NO widget-side keymap
decision_reason: Round-11 design memo D4: vendoring surface does NOT include a keymap. The keymap lives in the consumer frame dispatch. Round-11 example routes Arrow Up/Down + vim j/k/g/G/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn into ListState::select; Enter confirms selection; q/Esc quits. Diagnostic: the StatefulWidget vendoring should NEVER bundle its own keymap because (a) the consumer frame cycle has a global keymap already (round-8 example routes scroll keys to the active tab - adding a widget-side keymap on List would conflict with the global dispatch) and (b) the selection predicate ListState::select(Some(idx)) is the canonical consumption surface for any key mapping - vendoring a keymap surface would be redundant with the consumer frame dispatch. Round-11 vendored crate exports only ::select; the example TuiApp::handle_event chooses which keys map to it.
summary: Claim: D4 round-11 keymap: arrow + vim into ListState::select, NO widget-side keymap

The two patterns are structurally different and the layout reflects this - round-11 has NO TabNav surface because the List IS the navigation surface, not a sibling of it.

decision_title: D9 round-11 ingestion: per-tick ListState::select(Some(sel+1) % items.len()), deterministic + MSRV-portable + Instant-free
decision_reason: Round-11 design memo D9: selection-driven ScrollView composition. When items.len() > viewport.height, wrap List body in scroll_view.scroll_offset() + sync ListState::select(idx) -> scroll_state.offset.y. Per-tick ingest = state.select(Some(state.selected.unwrap_or(0).saturating_add(1) % items.len())) - NOTE: the modulo operand is on usize; usize is a stable operator in Rust 1.85.0 MSRV, so is_multiple_of cold-path does NOT apply (carries forward round-8 constitutional hazard #1 solved). The 12-cell ingest-precedent from round-10 D9 (deterministic tick_count ring) is replaced by a deterministic selection-step. Carry forward all three round-8 constitutional hazards: (1) MSRV is_multiple_of cold-path - solved by usize modulus; (2) Path B umbrella-bypass - round 11 plans vendoring + umbrella feature + example in same PR, no Path B debt; (3) Instant::now() test-loop trap - vendoring tests never read wall-clock. Diagnostic: selection-driven scroll composition is the round-11 novel compositional surface - List selection carrier (ListState.selected) projects onto scroll-view offset (scroll_state.offset.y), so the canonical carrier (ListState) drives a derived projection (scroll_state.offset.y). This is the round-11 carry-forward to all future stateful-widget compositions.
summary: Claim: D9 round-11 ingestion: per-tick ListState::select(Some(sel+1) % items.len()), deterministic + MSRV-portable + Instant-free

E0034 fully-qualified-vs-submodule carve-out — bare `list.render(area, buf)` triggers E0034 "multiple applicable items in scope" when both Widget::render and StatefulWidget::render are in scope on the same type. Canonical disambiguation patterns: Pattern A — fully qualified `<List as StatefulWidget>::render(list, area, buf, &mut state)` at the call site; Pattern B — keep the StatefulWidget impl in a submodule (tornado_list::stateful) so only one impl is in scope at the consumer import path. NEVER bare-method-call at vendored-crate call sites. The round-11 crates/tornado-list/src/lib.rs module-level doc-comment captures both patterns and warns explicitly against the bare method-call form. Diagnostic: the canonical StatefulWidget-vendoring precedent (D2) requires both impls in the same crate, and Rust method-call resolution collapses both render signatures into a single `render` symbol on the `List` type. Without either disambiguation pattern, every adopter of a StatefulWidget surface would hit E0034. The round-11 doc-comment is the canonical reference for any future stateful-widget round (Chart, Calendar, Pane).
